name: Carni to Gogoplata Setup
summary: A Carni-to-Gogoplata setup changes a shoulder-lock configuration into a shin-under-chin choke setup, requiring a new leg angle and safe release of the captured arm.
description: A Carni-to-Gogoplata setup changes a shoulder-lock configuration into a shin-under-chin choke setup, requiring a new leg angle and safe release of the captured arm.
overview:
The bottom player has a Carni shoulder connection and must reorganize the high leg while keeping posture close. The shin must actually pass under the chin. Carni shoulder pressure alone is not a Gogoplata, and a blocked chin is a reason to reset rather than grind the face.

Remove wrist and triceps finishing pressure before changing the leg angle. Keep a comfortable knee hug and hip connection as the opponent's arm is released. Use a forearm frame and hip turn to make room for the high leg.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Richie Martinez — Carni shoulder lock from Z guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iClQ2Np-n30); [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs).

The new shin-under-chin enclosure prepares the Gogoplata's throat compression. In this setup drill, stop at placement and release before adding choke pressure.

attacker.name: Carni to Gogoplata Setup Attacker
attacker.description: Carni to Gogoplata Setup (attacker): Remove wrist and triceps finishing pressure before changing the leg angle. Keep a comfortable knee hug and hip connection as the opponent's arm is released.
attacker.overview:
The bottom player has a Carni shoulder connection and must reorganize the high leg while keeping posture close. The shin must actually pass under the chin. Carni shoulder pressure alone is not a Gogoplata, and a blocked chin is a reason to reset rather than grind the face.

Remove wrist and triceps finishing pressure before changing the leg angle. Keep a comfortable knee hug and hip connection as the opponent's arm is released. Use a forearm frame and hip turn to make room for the high leg.

Use the available path without hauling the foot against a fixed knee. Stop at a controlled shin-under-chin enclosure; do not substitute jaw pressure. Return to guard if the opponent recovers posture or the shin cannot enter comfortably.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Release the Carni rotational lock before placing the shin under the chin. The neck frame and supported hip turn change the target from shoulder to throat; maintaining the old triceps tension while moving the leg would load two different structures at once.

As the shoulder clamp opens, keep the inside forearm between the bodies to manage incoming chest pressure while the shin changes position. McCaghren shows this barrier preventing the top player from crushing the space needed for the shin-under-chin enclosure.

flashcards.question: Carni to Gogoplata (bottom): Which pressure must end before the leg changes position?
flashcards.answer: Remove the Carni shoulder-lock pressure before changing the high leg toward the neck.

plausible: Only the foot pressure on the mat
Only your lower butterfly hook
trap: Only the forearm frame beside the neck

flashcards.question: Carni to Gogoplata (bottom): What helps keep the opponent close as the arm is released?
flashcards.answer: Retain comfortable knee support and hip connection as the Carni arm is released.
flashcards.answer_line: A supported knee hug with close hip connection

plausible: An extended arm pulling the trapped wrist
Flat hips with the high knee drifting away
trap: An ankle pulled upward against a fixed knee

flashcards.question: Carni to Gogoplata (bottom): How do you preserve room for the shin to move?
flashcards.answer: An inside forearm frame blocks incoming chest pressure while hip rotation creates room for the high leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Place the forearm inside and turn the hips

plausible: Lay the forearm outside the incoming chest
Stay flat and pull harder on the foot
trap: Drop the inside frame before making room for the shin

flashcards.question: Carni to Gogoplata (bottom): The knee is fixed and the foot cannot enter; what changes first?
flashcards.answer: Move through available space with a supported knee; if the foot cannot enter, release and adjust rather than hauling it.
flashcards.answer_line: Release tension and adjust the hips

plausible: Pull the foot inward without moving the hips
Raise the foot while keeping the same hip angle
trap: Release the hand grip but keep the knee wedged

flashcards.question: Carni to Gogoplata (bottom): Where must the shin lie for the intended neck enclosure?
flashcards.answer: The setup requires actual shin placement beneath the chin; the training checkpoint omits finishing pressure.
flashcards.answer_line: Under the chin against the front of the neck

plausible: Across the closed jaw in front of the neck
Behind the head against the upper neck
trap: Across the upper chest below the throat

flashcards.question: Carni to Gogoplata (bottom): The opponent sits upright before shin entry; what do you rebuild?
flashcards.answer: If posture escapes or comfortable shin entry is unavailable, return to guard instead of forcing the switch.
flashcards.answer_line: Facing guard with frames between the bodies

plausible: A head grip with both knees left outside
The old wrist grip with the shoulder already free
trap: A shin reach toward the chin from distant hips

flashcards.question: Carni to Gogoplata (bottom): Which connection describes the starting Carni position?
flashcards.answer: The starting threat is a shoulder clamp; release its load before building a different neck enclosure.
flashcards.answer_line: A leg-assisted shoulder clamp with arm control

plausible: A high shin grip with the opposing arm still free
A shin beneath the chin with the shoulder released
trap: A both-arm leg triangle around the shoulder line

flashcards.question: Carni to Gogoplata (bottom): Which target changes when the new setup is established?
flashcards.answer: Carni controls the shoulder; Gogoplata requires a separate shin-under-chin neck enclosure.
flashcards.answer_line: The shoulder lock becomes a shin-based neck enclosure

plausible: The shin keeps levering the upper arm against the overhook
The crossed legs compress the torso while the neck stays free
trap: The supported foot pushes the captured shoulder farther behind the back

flashcards.question: Carni to Gogoplata (bottom): In the setup-only drill, the shin stays on the jaw; what next?
flashcards.answer: A blocked chin is a failed entry for this drill. Reset without grinding the jaw or restoring shoulder-lock pressure.
flashcards.answer_line: Abandon the choke setup and recover guard space

plausible: Keep the head grip and increase pressure on the jaw
Keep the shin on the jaw and pull the head lower
trap: Reapply wrist pressure while leaving the shin on the jaw

defender.name: Carni to Gogoplata Setup Defender
defender.description: Carni to Gogoplata Setup (defender): Use an inside forearm frame before the shin enters under the chin. Do not jerk the head upward while the high leg remains fixed.
defender.overview:
The bottom player has a Carni shoulder connection and must reorganize the high leg while keeping posture close. The shin must actually pass under the chin. Carni shoulder pressure alone is not a Gogoplata, and a blocked chin is a reason to reset rather than grind the face.

Use an inside forearm frame before the shin enters under the chin. Do not jerk the head upward while the high leg remains fixed. Recover the elbow as the shoulder lock opens, without yanking against remaining control.

Avoid driving the partner into a neck stack during the leg change. Stop if the shin and head control already close the neck space. Rebuild upright posture once the head-side leg and arm connection have opened.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Make the early escape during the release of the shoulder clamp, before the shin and hand form the new neck enclosure. Keep a balanced posture and deny the space under the chin without driving the partner's high knee sideways.
key_principles: Protect the chin line early: Use an inside forearm frame before the shin enters under the chin.
Avoid a forced posture pull: Do not jerk the head upward while the high leg remains fixed.
Track the arm release: Recover the elbow as the shoulder lock opens, without yanking against remaining control.
Keep a safe base: Avoid driving the partner into a neck stack during the leg change.
Tap to an enclosed choke: Stop if the shin and head control already close the neck space.
Recover after the leg clears: Rebuild upright posture once the head-side leg and arm connection have opened.

flashcards.question: Carni to Gogoplata (top): What blocks the shin's entry before it reaches your chin?
flashcards.answer: Use an inside forearm early to preserve space before the shin and head control form a neck enclosure.
flashcards.answer_line: An inside forearm frame between the bodies

plausible: A forearm outside the high knee and chest gap
A palm on the hip with the elbow outside the gap
trap: A wrist grip with the forearm pulled behind the torso

flashcards.question: Carni to Gogoplata (top): Your head-side leg connection is still fixed; how do you regain height?
flashcards.answer: Rebuild posture after the head-side leg connection opens, not by pulling upward through it.
flashcards.answer_line: Clear that connection before raising the head

plausible: Raise the chest while the head-side leg stays connected
Turn the chin away before the shoulder clears
trap: Lower the opponent's free leg and then lift the head

flashcards.question: Carni to Gogoplata (top): When can your elbow return toward the ribs?
flashcards.answer: Recover the elbow during the released shoulder phase, before the new neck enclosure closes.
flashcards.answer_line: As the clamp opens and the arm frees

plausible: While the triceps and wrist remain fixed
Only after the shin closes under the chin
trap: By straightening the elbow against the clamp

flashcards.question: Carni to Gogoplata (top): Which support avoids folding the partner onto the neck during the change?
flashcards.answer: Keep balanced support and allow the shoulder and leg connections to clear without stacking the partner.
flashcards.answer_line: Balanced support without driving their hips over the neck

plausible: Forward weight carrying their hips beyond their shoulders
Pressure through their knees toward their forehead
trap: Circling while their raised hips rest on the neck

flashcards.question: Carni to Gogoplata (top): The shin and head grip have closed the neck space; what now?
flashcards.answer: Once the neck enclosure is secure, tap and obtain release rather than relying on late head movement.
flashcards.answer_line: Tap and have the neck enclosure released

plausible: Keep lifting the chin inside the closed grip
Turn the head beneath the retained shin
trap: Continue hand fighting as if the entry were still open
